probes.question: How were Roman roads built?
options: Layers of rubble, gravel and stone

probes.question: True or false: all of the 400,000 km of Roman roads were stone-paved.

image.alt: Low view across the large dark basalt paving stones of the ancient Appian Way, with ruined tombs and cypress and pine trees beside it.

body.question: At the peak of Rome's development, the empire's roads added up to more than...
body.reveal: More than 400,000 km, of which over 80,500 km were stone-paved. 29 great military highways radiated from Rome, and 372 great roads linked the empire's 113 provinces. Builders laid rubble, gravel and stone in layers.
